Mongoose's $expr caster drops the schema when it recurses into a non-literal right-hand operand (cast$expr.js castComparison calls _castExpression(val[1]) with no schema argument), so a comparison whose right side is another $cond containing a path/literal comparison throws TypeError: Cannot read properties of undefined (reading 'path') while the query is built. MongoDB itself evaluates $cond against $cond correctly, so a Mongoose fix would change this answer

The tags.exists lambda compares an element's name with the root document's aString. $elemMatch rebases every field path onto the array element, and the only route back to a root field is a $-anchored path inside $expr, which MongoDB rejects below the top level ('$expr can only be applied to the top-level document')

The categories.exists lambda reads the root document's tags collection from inside the element scope. $elemMatch rebases every field path onto the array element, and the only route back to a root field is a $-anchored path inside $expr, which MongoDB rejects below the top level ('$expr can only be applied to the top-level document')

gt aggregation expressions inside collec: MongoDB rejects $expr below the top level of a query ('$expr can only be applied to the top-level document'), and field arithmetic exists only as an aggregation expression inside $expr; the per-element scope this needs comes from $elemMatch, so no find filter is both element-scoped and expression-valued. It would take an aggregation pipeline ($map/$filter plus $anyElementTrue), which a Mongoose Query filter is not
contains aggregation expressions inside: Using an outer document field as the needle of a string search over an array element needs an aggregation expression over a $-anchored path, and MongoDB rejects $expr below the top level ('$expr can only be applied to the top-level document'), so it cannot sit inside the $elemMatch that scopes the element
ne aggregation expressions inside collec: Same top-level-only $expr restriction as p-ternary-in-exists, reached through all(): the negated $elemMatch that expresses all() still cannot contain the $cond aggregation expression the conditional needs
Unsupported operator inside aggregation: A bare ternary is planned as $expr/$cond, and an aggregation expression has no membership form here: MongoDB's $in aggregation operator raises a runtime error when its array operand is missing, which is exactly the absent-to-one-parent case this action probes, so lowering it would fail the whole query rather than deny the row
timestamp value must be a millisecond-ex: the planner emits a nanosecond-precision now() literal that BSON Date cannot represent without changing the CEL instant
same nanosecond-precision now() limitation in value-first form
Cannot tell numeric addition from string: a CONSTANT is what tells CEL's two `+` overloads apart, and between two field paths there is none. MongoDB spells the two differently — $add accepts numeric and date types only, $concat strings — and the mapper carries no field types, so neither can be chosen. Sending $add anyway is what the server aborts the whole query on, so the shape is refused at translation instead
Unsupported operator inside aggregation: Mongoose handles map() only as the collection operand of hasIntersection, where it becomes an $elemMatch. Comparing the projection itself to a literal list would need $map inside an aggregation expression, which the adapter's expression builder has no case for
hierarchy separator must be a non-empty: The hierarchy operand parser refuses an empty separator before the anchored `^prefix + separator` regex is built: with an empty separator that regex would match the path itself (a2, never its own descendant) as well as every string extension of it
